chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you enter the mosque and the Imam is bowing, and you think that if you walk to him he will raise his head before you catch up with him, then say Takbir and bow; when he raises his head, prostrate in your place; when he stands, join the row; and when he sits, sit in your place; and when he stands, join the row."

And in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: And he mentioned the like of it.
The Takbir of bowing suffices for the Takbir of opening for one who fears missing the bowing; he narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if they enter the mosque while the Imam is already bowing?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical jurisprudence of joining a congregational prayer (*fath al-salat*) when the worshipper arrives during the Imam's bowing (*ruku'*). It highlights the Shia scholarly consensus that the single bowing and prostration performed in place suffice for the missed *ruku'*, and the accompanying *takbir* serves as the *takbirat al-iftitah*, ensuring the validity of the partial prayer without requiring the worshipper to rush disruptively.
